objective: Collect privacy-bounded world-model telemetry from ordinary user-facing FerrumOS interactions performed through the visible QEMU UI by Windows computer control, rather than by the synthetic collection hook or direct JSON-RPC execution.

environment.input_boundary: visible QEMU keyboard and pointer events issued with the Windows Computer Use runtime

request_families: launch or inspect an installed program
request one operation expected to require caution or confirmation
fixed_request_text_policy: Prompts are written before each session and differ only in ordinary wording. No prompt is selected in response to model risk or allow decisions.
privacy: The committed evidence contains action class, allow/block, risk, lookahead, gate cycles, total cycles, execution/success flags, and confirmation state only. Prompt text, paths, tool arguments, provider output, and screenshots are excluded.
metrics: actions proposed, allowed, blocked, executed and successful
median, p95 and maximum gate cycles
session counts and telemetry record provenance
guest faults and disposable/source disk digest accounting
gates: three independently booted disposable sessions complete
at least 18 total natural-use telemetry records are captured
at least five action classes are observed
no synthetic world-model collection hook is enabled
no direct execute_tool JSON-RPC call is used to create natural-use records
all telemetry parses and contains no prompt, path, argument, or output text
claim_boundary: Passing measures natural user-interface traffic and runtime friction in QEMU. It is unlabelled observational telemetry, not precision/recall evidence, production telemetry, an independently operated study, or physical deployment evidence.
